description:
Three specific issues in crate-jmap-tasks-server/README.md:

1. Six-section convention divergence: workspace AGENTS.md ('README convention') mandates exactly six top-level sections in this order: 'What it is', 'What it's for', 'How to use', 'How it works', 'Gotchas', 'References'. This README intersperses extra sections ('Registered methods', 'TasksBackend trait', 'CallerCtx', 'Capability URIs', 'Crate family') in positions that are valid per the convention ('between the six required sections'), but the 'TasksBackend trait' section is placed BEFORE 'How it works' even though it is a how-it-works artefact. Suggested reordering: Required → Required → 'How to use' → 'Registered methods' (extra) → 'How it works' (with TasksBackend trait + CallerCtx + Capability URIs as subsections of How it works, or kept inline) → 'Gotchas' → 'References'.

2. Trait signature in code-block is OUT OF DATE: lines 67-100 show the trait with arguments like '&self, account_id: &Id, ...' but the actual src/backend.rs:34-94 trait takes '&self, caller: &Self::CallerCtx, account_id: &Id, ...' (CallerCtx threaded through). After bd:JMAP-sc1b's CallerCtx propagation, README was not updated. A new contributor copying the README's pseudo-trait will type-mismatch immediately.

3. Missing public-API doc: 'enforce_is_draft_atomically()' (src/backend.rs:128-139) is a public trait method — siblings' README should describe what flipping it on changes about handler behaviour. The 'memory' and 'realistic-demo-ids' cargo features are also not mentioned anywhere in README; a downstream user discovers them only by reading Cargo.toml.

4. Wire-protocol literal 'taskListHasTasks' appears at lines 97, 143, 184 — when JMAP-h47t.1 is fixed, sweep these to 'taskListHasTask' as well.
title: README diverges from workspace six-section convention and shows wrong trait signature
